assumptions: plm.source_resolution, plm.licensing_relationship_resolution and plm.licensing_source_scope each have RLS enabled with a policy granting authenticated SELECT, verified live via pg_class.relacl and has_table_privilege.
plm.opa_capture and plm.opa_property_character_capture grant SELECT to service_role only and carry no policy, so a browser role cannot read them at all.

Because those two tables are unreadable by a browser role, joining them into a security_invoker view returns a silent zero rather than a denial, which is why OPA corroboration is exposed as a guarded aggregate with an explicit opa_evidence_readable flag.
information_schema is permission-filtered in this project and under-reports, so every privilege assertion uses pg_class.relacl, has_table_privilege and pg_constraint instead.
The resolution tables are currently empty on production, so an empty read proves nothing and the security proof rests on privilege probes rather than row counts.
